newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia PM assures envoys on crisis, ASEAN entry.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia PM assures envoys on crisis, ASEAN entry.

text.p: Co-Premier Hun Sen assured diplomats that Cambodia's political crisis will not turn violent and vowed to ensure his nation's entry into the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), envoys said on Saturday.
"This should be a reassuring signal," said one Asian diplomat.
Hun Sen called diplomats to his country home outside Phnom Penh for a meeting late on Friday afternoon to discuss troubles with his co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh.
Diplomats at the meeting told Reuters that Hun Sen said he had taken steps to prevent violence between his Cambodian People's Party and Ranariddh's royalist FUNCINPEC party.
"He said there would be no coups... and said he had agreed with Ranariddh to ensure ASEAN agreements and requirements were expedited," said another diplomat who attended the meeting.
"We came out of the meeting feeling assured. I don't think there should be more concern about attempted coups," the diplomat said, adding that was "good news for investors and tourists."

Relations between the two leaders, who formed an uneasy coalition after U.N.-sponsored polls in 1993, have deteriorated since a deadly March 30 grenade attack on a demonstration led by Ranariddh's ally, opposition leader Sam Rainsy.
Tensions worsened last week when Hun Sen said he supported a challenge to Ranariddh's leadership by royalist dissidents, sparking rumours of an imminent coup.
But fears of a bloody climax to the political crisis appeared eased on Saturday, and acting head of state Chea Sim also called for calm and reconciliation at a speech at a hospital opening.
In a letter to the Khmer Journalists Association, King Norodom Sihanouk appealed to the two leaders to abide by the constitution to ensure the survival of the fragile democracy.
But analysts said that despite the easing of angry rhetoric between the two sides, disagreements over the monarchy, elections and power-sharing remain unresolved.
They predicted troubles between Ranariddh and Hun Sen would continue until coming elections, slated for 1997 and 1998. The two leaders are expected to oppose each other in the polls.

Despite its problems, Cambodia is expected to enter ASEAN along with Burma and Laos this year, analysts said. ASEAN groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
